answer: A saffron inlet guards an agent economy with a Mersenne channel: every new identity must be rowed through the inlet by a single harbor pilot, and the channel lengthens by one stroke more than doubling each time, so the first fake rows 1 stroke, the second 3, the third 7, the tenth 1,023 and the twentieth 1,048,575, and twenty fakes together row 2,097,130 strokes. Bulk farming fails because one pilot rows one boat and each crossing must finish before the next begins, so no stroke can be rowed in parallel or bought; like a ferryman feeling the pulse of the tide, one passenger at a time.
